previous_statement: Projection and nonvanishing transfer: node 1.1 says P_0 is a nontrivial delta-projection with delta=C_np*epsilon_X. By def-delta-projection, nontrivial means precisely that both P_0 and I_X-P_0 are nonvanishing; the same definition states that the complement of a delta-projection is again a delta-projection with the same delta when the algebra has exact unit. Here I_X is the original unit of the multiplication, hence exact and two-sided. Therefore the P_prime and P_doubleprime of node 1.2 are both nonvanishing C_np*epsilon_X-projections for the original product.
new_statement: Projection and nonvanishing transfer with coefficient enlargement: let C_base:=C_proj (the coefficient called C_np in node 1.1). The definition def-delta-projection supplies a universal complement-error coefficient, so there is a universal finite C_cmp>=0 for which the complement of a delta-projection in an epsilon_X-C*-algebra is a (delta+C_cmp*epsilon_X)-projection (the definition's delta+O(epsilon_X) clause). Set C_bar:=max{C_base,C_base+C_cmp}. Then the P_prime and P_doubleprime of node 1.2 are both nonvanishing C_bar*epsilon_X-projections for the original product.
